textual.context: The title and speech present the material as an online earning platform and describe the X3 plan and larger levels. The supplied records do not establish whether this is an advertisement, personal testimony, educational discussion, or another format.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised monetary return is linked to putting $5 into an X3 plan and opening larger levels, with marketing described as part of the activity; the relationship may require later assessment of the offer, payment flow, and stated conditions.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish who receives the money, what the levels contain, whether returns occurred, whether the platform is legitimate, or whether the claims are guaranteed or conditional beyond the quoted statements.

visual.observation: A promotional graphic for FORSAGE/WAGAS visibly states “100% PAYOUT” and describes the project as decentralized on a blockchain, alongside community branding.
visual.context: The claim appears in a branded promotional graphic; whether it is quotation, demonstration, or an offer is unclear from the sampled frame.
visual.potential_relevance: A specific payout claim is presented together with project branding and an apparent community affiliation, which conditionally merits review of how the promised payout relates to participation.
visual.limitations: The frame does not establish whether any payout occurred, what action or conditions are required, or whether the branding represents a verified organization or endorsement.

visual.observation: A FORSAGE presentation visibly explains “MATRIX MARKETING,” showing X3 and X4 placement diagrams and text referring to permanent reward sharing, automatic recycling, a limited number of places, and unlimited cycles.
visual.context: The material is presented as an explanatory marketing diagram, with red handwritten annotations visible in F0035; the purpose and audience of the presentation are otherwise unclear.
visual.potential_relevance: The presentation links stated rewards and repeated cycles to placement in a matrix structure and mentions limited places, creating a specific recruitment or participation-related relationship for conditional review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not show the full terms, payment steps, eligibility requirements, or whether the diagram describes an actual operating program.

visual.observation: A dashboard at “busd.forsage.io” shows the profile “MeharWagas,” a “Join Priority Leaders” button, a personal link labeled “forsage.io/b/hetzki,” profits of “8 621.3 BUSD,” and counts for partners and team members.
visual.context: The screen combines a personal referral link, a join prompt, reported profits, and partner/team counts in a logged-in-looking dashboard; the relationship between these items is presented visually but not independently explained.
visual.potential_relevance: A stated profit amount is displayed alongside a join action, personal referral destination, and recruitment-related partner/team counts, which is a concrete reward-and-recruitment relationship that conditionally merits review.
visual.limitations: The frame cannot establish that the displayed balance or profits are real, withdrawable, earned by the profile owner, or connected to any viewer action; the sampled URL was not followed.

visual.context: The screen visibly presents invitation information, a personal referral link, reported profits, and network counts; the red annotations appear to emphasize those dashboard fields.
visual.potential_relevance: Reported BUSD profits are shown together with an invitation relationship, referral link, and network-member counts, linking the return claim to recruitment or directed contact for conditional review.
visual.limitations: The frame does not establish the source, validity, accessibility, or outcome of the displayed funds, nor whether anyone used the referral link.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage BUSD through a matrix-marketing structure where participation and higher-level purchases are tied to earning more money. The speaker says viewers can put "$5 in X3" and that opening "big levels" will produce "a lot of money," while the displayed materials show matrix slots, upgrade payments, team counts, profits, and a personal Forsage link. These features together encourage participation in a recruitment- and tier-dependent earning scheme rather than merely discussing it.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S06 fits because the video presents Forsage's X3/X4 matrix structure, describes opening larger levels to obtain more money, and displays team and partner counts alongside earning figures. The evidence shows a multi-person hierarchy and an earnings relationship tied to matrix participation and level upgrades.
